As an ordinary formal scheme, the completion along $D$ has underlying topological space supported on $D$, so deleting that entire support gives the empty open formal subscheme (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0GXX and 0AHY). A punctured realization, an étale tube, or another precise meaning of the uncertain “ombre” is therefore required before the displayed object has the proposed content. This differs from the explicit torus-torsor model in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 121–123, which is a possible comparison object but not an automatic identification. Payne (2013, Remark 1.3) uses a nonarchimedean punctured tubular neighborhood, so complex-analytic circle tests must remain conditional on a different specified realization.

For the boundary-index convention $J\ne\varnothing$ and the complex punctured-tube realization, take $U=\mathbf P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$: all nonempty boundary strata are points, the maquette is three isolated vertices, and the punctured tube retracts onto three circles. Thus contractibility of those strata alone does not recover that full homotopy type, even for an elementary hyperbolic curve; the corresponding local étale inertia also retains procyclic factors. This adds an elementary test to, and agrees with, the circle-fiber data of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 80 and scans 121–123, while it does not contradict the different nonarchimedean boundary-complex interpretation described by Payne (2013, Remark 1.3). Confidence: high for the stated realization, because each local punctured complex disk retracts to $S^1$; no verdict is made for the unspecified literal “ombre” or a proviso including $D_\varnothing$.

The phrase “on doit avoir commutativité” specifies a compatibility requirement rather than demonstrating it. It adds a punctured-normal comparison to the composition square already imposed in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 118, (177), and to the two-cartesian, first-vertex-preserving comparisons on scan 132. Since these are groupoids, a proof should specify whether (234) commutes strictly or through a chosen natural isomorphism, and show that those isomorphisms satisfy the coherence required for longer flags.

For the proposed construction “par descente,” a concrete route would be to attach to each local embedded chart of $D'\to Y$ its cofiltered system of neighborhoods and then descend that system, retaining the transition isomorphisms on overlapping charts. This adds a possible construction to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 107–108, where the points of $D_d$ already remember a local branch germ, and to `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 242–245, where germs and their coverings are organized by filters. Confidence is medium: the local model is explicit, but effectiveness and presentation independence for the author's multiplicities still require proof, especially in light of scan 146's equivariant obstruction to choosing a normal-bundle parametrization.

“Des propriétés de transitivité tt à fait évidentes” still leaves the compatibility for a triple of local immersions to be specified. The assertion restates the transitivity aim of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 113–118, but adds punctured germs and the comparison with normal torsors, neither of which is supplied by the earlier categorical composition alone. Pullback on coverings gives a plausible coherent starting point, while transporting that structure through the equivalences in (239) requires compatible choices of those equivalences and their natural transformations.

The author now says that “croisements normaux” serves to express the germ groupoids in simpler terms, separating existence of generization from its torus description. This qualifies the formulation in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 133, where the missing half-simplicial structure was said to require normal-intersection hypotheses, while it develops the branch-torsor constructions of scans 121–123. In a local chart with $r$ coordinate branches, the complement has the meridians of $(\mathbb C^*)^r$; the remaining problem is descent with branch permutations and global twisting, not merely identifying each local fundamental group with $\mathbb Z^r$.

The theorem explicitly insists that one must not require “$D'\subset\Theta^{(d)*}$,” so it covers a stratum closure meeting deeper boundary strata. This adds a stronger comparison to the normal-torsor definitions on `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 122–127, and to the locally immersed flag geometry on scans 135–137. A proof must handle those deeper intersections and demonstrate an equivalence of the appropriate covering categories, not just compute a meridian group at a single smooth boundary point; scan 147's marginal reduction to $D'^{*}$ is itself a further assertion needing justification.

The tentative “il devrait être ‘assez évident’” asserts a noncanonical smooth normal-bundle model, while explicitly rejecting an analytic requirement. It adds a global, positive-codimension problem to the local coordinate germs with identity derivative used in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 259–260. The proof must distinguish existence of a smooth tubular parametrization, compatibility with the divisor, and independence of the induced covering functor; the last issue is addressed in the curve comparison by Deligne (1989, §§15.4–15.7), whereas the manuscript's larger-dimensional and quotient settings require additional arguments.

The transvection example can be checked directly if the uncertain upper-right matrix entry is the retained first reading $1$: the generator acts by $(x,y)\mapsto(x+y,y)$ and fixes the line $y=0$. An equivariant linear section of the quotient would send $1$ to a vector $(a,1)$ fixed by the generator, but that vector is sent to $(a+1,1)$, so the tangent extension does not split and an equivariant tubular diffeomorphism inducing the prescribed normal identification cannot exist. This adds an explicit verification to the proposed descent in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 259–260, where local coordinates have no such equivariance constraint; confidence is high conditional on the entry $1$, and the calculation is a test of the author's example rather than a claim of novelty.

The warning “c'est faux par contre dans le cas de multiplicités” suggests isolating a finite-stabilizer version of the failed construction. For a finite group acting smoothly on a paracompact manifold and preserving a closed embedded submanifold, averaging a Riemannian metric supplies an invariant metric, whose normal exponential map gives an equivariant tubular neighborhood after restricting its domain; this is a concrete mechanism absent for the displayed infinite transvection action. The proposal adds a conditional repair to the quotient-germ programme of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 78–80, and to the equivariance comparisons in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 263–264; confidence is high for the metric construction under the stated hypotheses, but it does not establish descent for arbitrary multiplicities or simultaneous compatibility with every boundary branch.

“On a oublié de préciser” records an additional condition: the tubular map must carry the relevant divisor complement to the punctured normal-bundle locus. This adds a compatibility requirement to the punctured line torsors of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 122–126, and explains why an arbitrary smooth tubular neighborhood cannot by itself prove (239). A local proof should track every coordinate hyperplane and then show that the compatible local models descend with the branch-permutation torsor; ordinary homotopy equivalence of the unpunctured spaces does not supply this condition.

The “flèche en sens inverse” compares a groupoid made from points and arcs with one made from coverings, and the author expressly omits the details. This restates, in a multibranch situation, the direction of the invariant functor $\Theta:\Pi_1(\mathbb S_x)\to\mathrm{Revuni}(D_x^*)$ constructed in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 256–262. A genuine construction should assign a fibre functor to each normal direction and transport along paths, then verify independence and composition; Deligne's curve result has the same comparison objective but explicitly treats the classical construction only for curves (Deligne, 1989, §15.3).
